name: Angela Merkel
summary: Merkel led Germany's governments for sixteen years as a pragmatic centre-right Christian Democrat. Her recorded outlook combines a social market economy and fiscal stability with strong commitments to the EU, NATO, multilateralism and free trade, and climate and equal-dignity themes. On several issues she changed course in office, including nuclear power after Fukushima and the 2017 marriage vote, and her line on migration moved from the 2015 welcome to limiting a repeat.

notes: Nuclear power: she extended nuclear lifetimes in 2010 but after Fukushima (2011) judged the risks not controllable and set the exit by 2022; the later position is recorded. Same-sex marriage: she opened a conscience vote in June 2017 but voted no, citing the Basic Law's definition of marriage; recorded as a mild no. Migration: the 2015 welcome ('Wir schaffen das', suspension of the Dublin rules) was followed by statements in 2016 that the situation should not be repeated, so the immigration level answer is neutral. Her full memoir 'Freedom' (2024) is not freely available, so it is used only through a review that quotes it. German-language texts were translated by the auditor. Where no source records her view, answers are null.
